output:
Short answer: pick a modern LED adjustable task/desk lamp that is dimmable, has a neutral-to-cool color temperature (≈3500–4000 K) and good efficacy (roughly 80–120 lm/W) — that combination gives the best energy efficiency and office visual comfort.

What to look for (practical spec targets)
- Light source: LED (far more efficient than incandescent/CFL).  
- Power and output: 5–12 W for typical desk tasks (choose higher output if you need very bright light). Aim for 300–1,000 lumens depending on task.  
- Efficacy: 80+ lm/W (higher = more light per watt).  
- Color temperature: 3500–4000 K for neutral white; 4000 K often preferred in offices.  
- CRI: ≥80 (90+ if color accuracy matters).  
- Controls: stepless dimming and multiple brightness levels.  
- Mounting: clamp or weighted base depending on desk space.  
- Extra energy features (optional): motion/occupancy sensor, built-in daylight sensor, USB charging only if needed.  
- Certifications: Energy Star or equivalent indicates verified efficiency.  
- Lifetime: rated 25,000–50,000 hours reduces replacement frequency.

Why these choices (evidence)
- LEDs use far less power for the same lumen output than incandescents (typical LED desk lamps draw 5–15 W vs 40–60 W for incandescent bulbs producing similar useful light).  
- Higher lm/W (efficacy) is the direct measure of energy efficiency: more lumens for each watt consumed.  
- Neutral/cool color temps (3500–4000 K) improve perceived brightness and focus in office tasks without being harsh.  
- CRI impacts how accurately colors render; office work and screen work benefit from CRI ≥80.  
- Dimming saves energy when full brightness isn’t needed. Motion sensors/daylight harvesting can reduce wasted on-time.

Catalog note and verification
- I found entries in the catalog memory for “Meadowlight Lamp” and several generic “adjustable desk lamps” / “task lamps,” but I don’t have provenance or detailed specifications for those items from the saved memory. That means I can’t confirm wattage, lumen output, CRI, color temp, Energy Star certification, price, warranty, or availability for any specific catalog item right now. Those are the claims you should verify on a product spec sheet before purchase.

Specific product suggestions (types, not unverified claims)
- Wide-panel LED task lamp with adjustable arm and dimmer (good for even illumination across a work area).  
- Focused head LED task lamp with high-efficacy LED (better if you need a concentrated beam).  
- Lamp with occupancy sensor and dimming for shared or rarely-used desks (maximizes energy savings).

Next steps I can take for you
- Narrow recommendations if you tell me budget, desk size, prefer clamp vs base, need USB or sensor features, or style.  
- Look up and compare specific models (including Meadowlight Lamp) and return full spec comparisons (wattage, lumens, lm/W, CRI, CCT, dims, certifications, warranty, price). I’ll flag any product claims that need independent verification (e.g., manufacturer lm/W figures, Energy Star status).
